content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then overshoot, followed by a sharp drop — suggesting overreaction to recent spikes.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model fails to anticipate gradual downward drift after peaks.
- Forecast bias is stronger in later days of the 30-day window, with model prices often 2–5% higher than true values.
- Model exhibits lag in recognizing downward momentum; true price drops occur before model adjusts.
- Overshoot after spikes is common — model reacts too aggressively to short-term volatility, then corrects too late.
- Horizon-specific error: 1–3 day lag in recognizing true trend direction; model often misreads 30-day trend as short-term momentum.
